LESSON: POLITE LANGUAGE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.3: Polite language
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Polite language, part of Listening and Speaking in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: why we should use polite language in day-to-day interactions. ● Engage in dialogue using polite language in class (please, thank you, may I?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify words that depict polite language in daily interactions,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Polite language in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use polite language in daily interactions,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Polite language in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. Appreciate the use of polite language in day-to- day interactions. ● Name words used to request, apologise and appreciate. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication to name the words. ● Tell why we should use polite language in day-to-day interactions. ● Engage in dialogue using polite language in class (please, thank you, may I? kindly,). Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech to engage in dialogue. ● Use appropriate polite language 1. Why do we use polite language? 2. When do we use polite language? 25 while. ● Role playing work done by family members. Learners could be assigned roles according to their functional abilities. ● Watch a video clip or listen to a recording on use of polite language. Light intensity could be adjusted for learners who are sensitive to light. ● Talk about pictures showing gestures on use of polite language.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Polite language in the Kenya CBC curriculum.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Polite language together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: Speaking as the learner engages in dialogue using polite language in class and role plays

work done by family members.

• Creativity and imagination is enhanced as the learner assumes the roles of different family members while using polite

language.

Values:
• Respect is developed as the learner uses polite language to interact, request, apologise and appreciate others in daily life.

• Love is developed as the learner purposes to maintain good relations with those around by using polite language.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Family conflicts under citizenship education are avoided by the learner with the awareness of using polite language to maintain

good social relations.

Link to other Learning Areas: Religious education where learners learn to apologise and use polite language in social

interactions.
